## Goal

Make the dev-only telemetry recorder cheap enough that it does not distort a measured run.

**User story:** As a developer profiling the game, I want the dev telemetry recorder to stay out of the frame budget, so a profile measures the game and not the recorder.

## Evidence (measured, AH-0MVXV0E8000937U5)

CPU profile of \`PlayScene\` level 10 demo (60 s, desktop headless Chromium), with the dev recorder enabled:

- \`sanitiseObject\` (\`src/telemetry/redact.ts:93\`) 0.18 % of the measured window, \`sanitise\` (\`src/telemetry/redact.ts:65\`) 0.15 %, \`utf8ByteLength\` (\`src/telemetry/devUpload.ts:180\`) 0.14 %, \`write\` (\`src/telemetry/sinks.ts:50\`) 0.08 %, \`deepFreeze\` (\`src/ai/botSnapshot.ts:459\`) 0.16 % — **~0.7 % of the window / ~7 % of JS**.
- The same run logged a skipped run-end upload: 15.8 MiB of run telemetry exceeded the 8 MiB browser→node message cap, so the recorder was serialising a payload it then discarded.

## Scope

- Avoid serialising/redacting a payload that will be discarded for exceeding the upload cap (check the size first, or stream/bound the recording).
- Keep redaction guarantees intact: no unredacted payload may ever reach a sink.

## Out of scope

- Production telemetry behaviour (the recorder is dev-only).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A run whose telemetry exceeds the upload cap no longer pays the full serialise+redact cost before discarding (verified by a test on the size-guard seam).
2. Redaction tests still pass (no path skips redaction for a payload that is written).
3. In the same profiled demo run, the telemetry bucket share is measurably lower, with the before/after numbers recorded on this item.
4. Full project test suite passes.

## Goal

Record and, if the producer authorises it, act on the **raster-side** lever that remains after AH-0MW2IRYAH0055WCN removed the last material per-frame `Graphics` draw submission.

**Discovered from:** AH-0MW2IRYAH0055WCN (mobile-tier shortfall).

## Measured situation

After AH-0MW2IRYAH0055WCN, a 60 s `GymPerformance` run at `--cpu-throttle 4` on the reference host (headless Chromium + SwiftShader) measures **24.3–24.6 FPS** against the ≥ 30 FPS mobile-tier bar (`docs/PERFORMANCE.md` → [Baked enemy body textures](docs/PERFORMANCE.md#baked-enemy-body-textures-ah-0mw2iryah0055wcn)). The draw-submission half is now small: main-thread JS fell 22.3 % → 15.9 % of the window and the renderer bucket 19.1 % → 12.2 %, but `native` rose to \~83 % and the frame time did not move. The whole enemy+bullet draw-submission surface is only ≈ 6.5 pp of the window, and `GymPlayer` (one Graphics, no enemies) already costs ≈ 24 ms/frame on this host.

Conclusion: the residual mobile-tier gap is **software rasterisation**, not draw submission. No further main-thread JS work can close it.

## Candidate levers (all need a producer decision — they change shipped rendering)

1. **Disable antialiasing** (`Phaser.Types.Core.GameConfig.antialias`, currently the Phaser default `true`; `src/core/gameConfig.ts` sets none). On SwiftShader, MSAA multiplies fragment work. This changes the shipped look on every platform, so it needs an explicit visual-quality decision (or a mobile-only render tier, which does not exist today).
2. **Render-scale / resolution tier** — render at a lower internal resolution on the mobile tier and upscale. Same decision class as (1).
3. **Hardware-GPU verification** — the mobile-tier bar is measured on a CPU rasteriser on this host; AH-0MW2IRYJ2006PV3P already tracks the hardware-GPU desktop runs. A hardware-GPU mobile-tier row would say whether the bar is met on real hardware (the likely answer, since the raster half is the SwiftShader artefact).

## Acceptance criteria

1. The producer decides which lever (if any) is authorised; the decision and its rationale are recorded on this item.
2. If a rendering-quality lever is authorised: it is measured with the same harness/throttle/window on the reference host, its before/after numbers and its visual-quality impact are recorded in `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`, and gym↔game parity is preserved (the setting lives in the shared game config, not per scene).
3. If hardware-GPU verification is chosen instead, record the mobile-tier result and its backend (`webgl.kind`) next to the SwiftShader row so the two are never confused.

## Out of scope

- Any further draw-submission optimisation (measured and exhausted by AH-0MW2IRYAH0055WCN).
- Changing the mobile target or the throttle factor.

## Goal (user story)

As an implementer of the blocked-pickup discard rule, I need unit tests that
pin the exact stick/throw contract *before* the behaviour exists, so the stepper
cannot drift once it is wired into the shared drop layer.

Parent: AH-0MW0UAQ23005AC9L. Producer answers Q1a/Q2a/Q3a are recorded in the
parent's Appendix and are authoritative here.

## Scope

Write the failing-first unit tests for the new pure stepper module
(`src/scenes/core/blockedDropDiscard.ts`, mirroring the existing
pure-logic-plus-thin-Phaser-seam pattern of `src/powerups/magnet.ts` and
`src/powerups/collectAnimation.ts`). Tests use structural doubles only — no
Phaser import, no scene instantiation — and an injected `rng` so every case is
deterministic.

This item and its implementation sibling (the feature child that follows it)
land together; the pair must be committed and pushed before the `dev` push gate
so the tree is never pushed red.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Unit tests for the blocked-discard stepper are created in `src/scenes/core/blockedDropDiscard.test.ts` and do not import Phaser or instantiate a scene.
- A case pins that the 1.5 s stick window starts on the **first frame** the blocked drop overlaps the ship and elapses only after 1.5 s of accumulated `dt` (producer Q1a): 1.49 s of accumulated `dt` never launches the drop, 1.5 s does.
- A case pins that a blocked drop that is **not** overlapping the ship accumulates no stick time.
- A case pins that while sticking the drop's `x`/`y` track the ship every frame, and the same test drives the stepper with **zero** Magnet stacks to prove the stick does not depend on the Magnet power-up (producer Q2a).
- A case pins that after the window the stepper records a **unit-length** direction taken from the injected `rng` and marks the drop as discarding (no `Math.random()` anywhere in the stepper).
- A case pins that a discarding drop advances `BLOCKED_DROP_THROW_SPEED × dt` along its stored direction and is removed from the kept list once it reaches **any** of the four screen edges (left, right, top and bottom each covered).
- A case pins that a drop that becomes collectable during the stick window is never thrown and its stick state is cleared (producer Q3a).
- A case pins that stick state is cleared on collection and on run restart, so a half-thrown drop cannot survive a new run.
- One deterministic seeded run asserts the direction varies across seeds (not a fixed vector), without asserting a specific distribution.
- Tests are run through the test skill (`/skill:test`, changed scope) and every new test's failure message names the behaviour it pins.
- No production scene outside the shared core gains stick/throw code.


**Parent acceptance criteria covered (restated verbatim where possible):**

- The tests pin that the drop refused by the six-slot collection gate sticks to the ship and moves with it for 1.5 s, starting from the first frame it overlaps the ship while blocked (producer Q1a).
- The tests pin that the launched drop travels in a straight line and is destroyed/removed when it reaches a screen edge.
- The tests pin that if a slot frees during the 1.5 s stick window the drop is collected normally and the throw is cancelled (producer Q3a).
## Constraints

- UK English in test names, comments and any failure messages.
- Agents must not invoke test commands directly; every run goes through the test skill.
- Use `RNG`/constant injection rather than timers: the stepper takes `dt`, so no fake clocks are required.

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/core/blockedDropDiscard.test.ts` — the new unit suite
- `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.test.ts` — sibling suite for the collection seam that starts the stick

- `src/core/constants.ts` — tunables the tests read (`BLOCKED_DROP_STICK_SECONDS`, `BLOCKED_DROP_THROW_SPEED`, `GAME_WIDTH`, `GAME_HEIGHT`)
